thread:
incident-bot: INCIDENT ALERT: decode-prod-1 pool reporting repeated CUDA OOMs + container crashes, ~7% request drops. Paging @alice_oncall :rotating_light:

alice_oncall: I'm on it. Observability dashboards show sudden increase in DecodeError/CUDA across nodes 10-14. Any recent deploys?

ben_runtime: no deploys in last 2 hours. I'm seeing a surge of very long token requests from a handful of API keys. Looks like a misconfigured client is passing max_tokens=100000 in some batched calls.

carla_sre: logs pulled from node-12 earlier: 
```
[2026-03-15T09:42:11Z] decode-node-12 kernel: Out of memory: Killed process 4321 (python) total-vm: 2456784kB, anon-rss: 1032540kB
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "server.py", line 202, in generate
    tokens = model.decode(...)
RuntimeError: CUDA error: out of memory
```

carla_sre: pod restart count spiked from 0 -> 4 in last 6m on the decode pool.

dan_support: any customer impact metrics? which tenants affected?

ben_runtime: preliminary filtering: ~12 distinct API keys, top three account for 78% of the dropped requests. Pattern: chat endpoint with unbounded user prompt and max_tokens absent or huge. We see streaming sessions never terminate.

elaine_cs: flagged customers: cust-omega (high impact), cust-beta (medium). I'm drafting a notice but need ETA for mitigation.

alice_oncall: mitigation plan: 1) temporarily route traffic from decode-prod-1 to decode-prod-2 with lower-capacity nodes and enforced token caps; 2) enable immediate token-level throttling on ingress for suspect keys; 3) apply hotpatch to validate and clamp max_tokens per-request to 2048. Who can do (1)/(2) now?

ben_runtime: I can flip routing rules. Doing `rb route apply` now to move 20% of streaming traffic off pool-1 -> pool-2 with fallback.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: reroute-policy/v2026.03.15-quickfix by ben_runtime (id: d-9912)

ben_runtime: reroute applied. Watching errors...

carla_sre: running `kubectl get pods -n decode -o wide` shows node-12 evicted earlier, node-13 restarted, node-14 flappy. CPU fine, memory balloon due to cuda allocs.

ben_runtime: enabling token throttling for suspect keys via feature flag: `feature.token_quota.enforce=true` and adding per-request clamp: `max_tokens_clamp=2048`. Pushing hotpatch.

deploy-bot: hotpatch rolled: token-clamp/v1.0 by ben_runtime (id: hp-334)

alice_oncall: Can someone attach the exact ingress rule we used so CS can reference it in comms?

ben_runtime: ingress change: 
```
- match: route.decode.streaming
  condition: api_key in [list_suspect_keys]
  action: set_max_tokens=2048, throttle=rate(5r/s)
  fallback: route=decode-prod-2
```

dan_support: confirmed: dropped request count decreasing from 7% -> 1.2% over last 4 minutes after routing + clamps. Cust-omega still seeing elevated errors but lower.

elaine_cs: I'll send an interim note to cust-omega: "we observed elevated GPU OOMs caused by unusually long generation requests; we have mitigations active and are continuing to stabilize. ETA 30-45m for full remediation." Any objections?

frank_prod: add note that we applied temporary token cap of 2048 and rerouted traffic; full fix will validate max_tokens on server-side permanently.

alice_oncall: Agreed. Next: node remediation. Carla, please collect heap/kv cache snapshots. Ben, can you proactively evict large KV entries?

carla_sre: collecting `nvidia-smi pmon -c 1` and memory maps. Also taking /dmesg and container logs.

ben_runtime: running eviction: `rb kvcache evict --age>7d --size>50MB --pool=decode-prod-1` and applying a soft-limit to KV cache per-session.

carla_sre: node-12 shows kernel-level OOM killer activity tied to python process that leaked GPU memory: PID 4321. I grabbed full stack and uploaded to /tmp/oom-traces/5100009876.txt

alice_oncall: Good. After stabilization we'll roll a server-side validation to reject requests with max_tokens>8192 by default and make that configurable per-tenant. For immediate followup, set SLO to prevent further bursts — add a global circuit breaker threshold at 3% dropped over 5m to automatically scale decode pool by +2 nodes.

ben_runtime: queued auto-scale rule: `policy.decode.spike=scale_out+2@3pct_errors/5m` (applied)

deploy-bot: autoscale-policy updated (id: sp-88)

dan_support: Customer impact timeline for the postmortem: start 09:42:11 UTC incident raised, 09:45:00 reroute & clamp applied, 09:49:30 drops down to 1.2%. Nodes stabilized 09:58:00 after eviction + restarts. Will that be enough for CS notes?

elaine_cs: yes, that's perfect. I'll file the customer update and follow up with a deeper RCA + permanent fix ETA in 24-48h.

frank_prod: Action items assigned: (1) Ben: implement server-side max_tokens validation + tests (owner, 24h). (2) Carla: attach kernels, dmesg, and KV snapshots to incident ticket (owner, 6h). (3) Support/CS: customer notices (owner, 30m). (4) SRE: review autoscale thresholds and rollback risk (owner, 12h).

alice_oncall: Good work. I'll start the incident doc and close paging once nodes remain stable for 20m. If drop rate creeps above 3% re-open page.

incident-bot: INCIDENT NOTE: severity reduced to P2 at 09:55:12 UTC. Auto-closure scheduled if metrics stable for 20m.
